What the headline value measures: Largest single invoice cited (2023); total described as tens of millions
Units (as described): At least 21 shipments to freight forwarders in Singapore and Malaysia
Charges / legal basis: Conspiracy to violate the Export Control Reform Act and the Export Administration Regulations (50 U.S.C. 4819(a), (b)); single-count indictment
Methods described: Company formed weeks after Oct 2022 controls; shipments to freight forwarders as false end users; payments from China/Hong Kong; mislabeled goods.
Notes, disputes & open questions: Funds column left blank: the only figure is one example payment ($1M from a China-based company, Jan 2024), not a total. Case name: US v. Ho, Raymond, Li & Chen (Janford Realtor)
Court / authority: M.D. Fla. (Senior Judge Charlene Edwards Honeywell)
Hardware named: Nvidia A100; H100 (in 10 HPE supercomputers); H200
What the headline value measures: Wire transfers from China funding the scheme (reported ~$3.89M; DOJ: nearly $4M)
Units (as described): 400 A100s exported in two shipments; two further shipments (10 HPE supercomputers with H100s; 50 H200s) disrupted
Charges / legal basis: Conspiracy to violate ECRA; ECRA violations; smuggling; money laundering and conspiracy
Methods described: Front company posing as a realtor; fake contracts and false end uses in Malaysia/Thailand; false Electronic Export Information.
Notes, disputes & open questions: Raymond is described in the indictment as owner of a distributor licensed to sell Nvidia GPUs. DOJ states no value for the 400 exported A100s. Ho pleaded guilty (docket); the other three defendants are set for trial in the term beginning 6 Jan 2027.

Case name: US v. Hsu / Hao Global; Yuan; Gong (Operation Gatekeeper)
Court / authority: S.D. Tex. (Judge Lee H. Rosenthal: Hsu and Hao Global; Judge Kenneth M. Hoyt: Yuan and Gong)
What the headline value measures: Nvidia H100/H200 GPUs exported or attempted to be exported (DOJ: "at least $160 million"); agreed purchase price of the full order was $160,815,000
Units (as described): 3,872 H100 + 3,160 H200 agreed purchase; relabeled 'SANDKYAN' in a New Jersey warehouse
Charges / legal basis: Hsu: smuggling, false export information. Yuan: conspiracy to violate ECRA. Gong: conspiracy to smuggle.
Methods described: Straw purchasers; relabeling to a fake brand; misclassification as 'adapter modules'; sham inspections; payments via Southeast Asian shell companies.
Notes, disputes & open questions: Payments were routed through intermediaries in Thailand, Singapore, Malaysia, China and Taiwan (The Wire China). Hsu and Hao Global pleaded guilty on 10 Oct 2025 (unsealed 8-9 Dec 2025); DOJ called it the first AI-diversion conviction. Hsu's sentencing has been reset several times (18 Feb, 5 Mar, 19 Aug and 16 Dec 2026) and is now set for 26 May 2027 on an agreed motion; his plea agreement provides that the government will ask for sentencing to be deferred until his cooperation is complete. The ~$50M recorded as reaching China comes from the Houston Chronicle; no official source stating a delivered value has been found. DOJ separately states more than $50M in wire transfers from the PRC and more than $50M in "Nvidia technologies and cash" seized. Hsu's maximum is 10 years on the smuggling count and 5 years on the export-information count, which may run consecutively (plea agreement); this explains the 10- vs 15-year figures in reporting. In Yuan's case the court suppressed certain evidence and barred Hsu's testimony in June 2026; the government has appealed to the Fifth Circuit (Nos. 26-20384, 26-20414).

Case name: US v. Liaw, Chang & Sun (Super Micro-linked)

Charges / legal basis: Conspiracy to violate ECRA; conspiracy to smuggle; conspiracy to defraud the US. Sun also pleaded to obstruction.
Methods described: Dummy replica servers; serial labels moved with hair dryers; repackaging into unmarked boxes; transshipment via a pass-through customer.
Notes, disputes & open questions: $510M is the value explicitly alleged to have reached China (Apr-May 2025). Bloomberg reported the pass-through company is OBON (Bangkok), which is not charged. Super Micro is not a defendant; it says it was a victim and an internal probe found no evidence current senior management knew. Indictment filed 17 Mar 2026 and unsealed 19 Mar 2026 (docket). The DOJ release refers to "the U.S. Manufacturer" and does not name Super Micro.

Charges / legal basis: Criminal conspiracy (18 U.S.C. 371) with objects of violating ECRA (50 U.S.C. 4819) and smuggling (18 U.S.C. 554); charged by information after waiver of indictment
Methods described: Thai companies named as purchasers; fake corporate materials; false Advanced Computing and End User Certifications.

The three defendants were charged in separate cases.

Charges / legal basis: Conspiracy to violate ECRA/EAR; outbound smuggling; conspiracy to commit money laundering

Docket / reference: Not found (Keelung District Prosecutors Office indictment, 24 Aug 2026; Keelung District Court)
Hardware named: Super Micro servers with Nvidia B300
What the headline value measures: Illicit profit that prosecutors say the organizers made after deducting payments to Albatron (US$21,205,531; about NT$675M)
Units (as described): 130 servers obtained; 74 reached China; 56 intercepted by customs
Charges / legal basis: Breach of trust; document forgery; embezzlement (some); aggravated breach of trust under Securities and Exchange Act (three)
Methods described: Fake end user (data-center lease quotation); Nvidia whitelist and on-site inspection defeated; Japanese shell company; fake websites.
Notes, disputes & open questions: Exporting to China in breach of US controls is not itself a crime in Taiwan, so prosecutors used other charges. Prosecutors sought 5 years (the statutory maximum) for four defendants including the Nvidia manager, and between 18 months and 6 years overall; the 6-year request relates to the separate Albatron embezzlement count (CNA, LTN). Investigation began after the Coast Guard uncovered suspected exports; searches from 20 May 2026. Conduct start is approximate (buyer whitelisted Feb 2025). Per CNA and LTN, eight people are charged over the servers and one further person only in the related Albatron embezzlement part. Keelung District Court held preparatory hearings on 16 Oct and 16 Nov 2026; one defendant denied the charges (udn). No trial date reported.

Hardware named: Servers that may contain Nvidia chips (from Dell, Super Micro, Asus)
Destination named: Malaysia (per Singapore government); any onward destination not established
Units (as described): 917 servers bought from Aperia International by two companies in 41 transactions
Charges / legal basis: Individuals: fraud by false representation and conspiracy (Penal Code ss 424B, 120B); money laundering (CDSA s 54); fraudulent trading (IRDA s 238(4)); abetment offences under the Computer Misuse Act and Companies Act (one defendant). Companies: fraud by false representation (s 424B); acquiring benefits of criminal conduct (CDSA s 54(3)).
Methods described: Alleged false statements to server makers about who the end user would be.
Notes, disputes & open questions: Singapore does not enforce other countries' export controls, so charges are for fraud. Prohibition-of-disposal order on a ~S$55M bungalow; ~S$1M seized (not converted). First charges 27 Feb 2025 (SPF). Next court date for newest defendants 4 Jan 2027. Do not assume defendant Li Ming is the same person as a 'Li Ming' named in reporting on Megaspeed. Singapore's home affairs minister said the servers went to Malaysia, "from Singapore to a country other than China," and "may contain Nvidia chips" (MHA transcript, Mar 2025). Victims named by SPF: Dell, Super Micro and Asus. The 4 Jan 2027 court date is from news reports.
